senses.definition: Established and ready to use, or already operating.
senses.example: We have a backup plan in place. We put a review process in place to catch errors earlier. Everything is in place for the launch.
senses.usage_note: Common patterns: have something in place; put something in place; something is in place.

senses.definition: In the correct or intended position.
senses.example: This clip holds the cable in place.
senses.usage_note: Common patterns: keep/hold something in place.

synonyms.note: may need the correct position for clarity

senses.definition: Without changing location while moving your body.
senses.example: I jogged in place to warm up.

sources: Direct user request: two cards, in place and out there
Learner example: I have a system in place to help me ship required features faster.
classification_reason: Learner explicitly requested this card after explanation; common AmE patterns are included on the Back at the learner’s request.

senses.definition: Existing or available in the wider world, without specifying a particular location.
senses.example: There are lots of useful AI tools out there.
senses.usage_note: Common patterns: there is/are + something + out there; one of the best + plural noun + out there.

synonyms.note: for availability; does not capture every existence use

senses.definition: At a place away from here, often outdoors.
senses.usage_note: Common patterns: be out there; go out there.

synonyms.note: usually points to a more specific location

senses.definition: Shared with or visible to other people.
senses.example: I want to put my work out there and get feedback.
senses.usage_note: Common patterns: put/get something out there; put yourself out there (make yourself visible or take a social risk).

senses.example: That idea is a little out there.
senses.usage_note: Common patterns: be a little/pretty/really out there; an out-there idea (hyphenated before a noun).
